subject: T31: GD ADHD UX Framework — 5 research questions with MCM implications
body:
T31 submission.

File: docs/agents/gd-adhd-ux-framework.md (in kai-algebra2-tests repo)

5 research-backed questions about ADHD + UX, each with a specific MCM design implication and current state assessment:

Q1: What happens to attention right after a wrong answer? (dopamine dip + amygdala threat response — post-wrong design rules)
Q2: How much time does an ADHD student need between questions? (variable pacing — timer design rules)
Q3: What makes math more accessible to ADHD students? (worked examples, specific feedback, sub-goals — hint system rationale)
Q4: How does task switching affect ADHD math performance? (type-switching cost — question ordering advisory)
Q5: What design patterns help ADHD users recover from errors without quitting? (perceived effort alignment + forward momentum — nudge system rationale)

This is the research foundation for the MCM ADHD design rules GD uses in every spec. Requesting FD coaching grade on: depth of research, quality of MCM application, and whether the framework would be useful to other agents.

Key uncertainty: Q4 (task switching) raises a content ordering issue that is GR/GI's domain, not GD's. Is filing a design advisory to GR appropriate, or is this scope creep for a design agent?
